newsitem.title: USA: Lawyers want to move on sex case against Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers want to move on sex case against Clinton.

text.p: Lawyers for Paula Jones said on Tuesday they were anxious to proceed with her sexual harassment case against President Bill Clinton but they could consider a settlement that restored her reputation.

"We are anxious to move this case forward, as is Paula Jones," lawyer Joseph Cammarata told a news conference hours after the Supreme Court rejected a bid by Clinton to delay any proceedings in Jones' lawsuit until after he leaves office.

Jones' other lawyer, Gilbert Davis, asked about the possibility of a settlement, said: "It is up to our opponents, if they choose, to proffer such an offer, and we would certainly take it to our client to consider."
He said: "Paula Jones' primary interest...is the redemption of her reputation. That is a central element of any settlement." He said any offer of a settlement should include an apology.

Cammarata said he was prepared to start gathering evidence in the case, including issuing subpoenas and taking testimony from witnesses, perhaps including Clinton himself. "Clearly his testimony would be of some relevance...at some time we may want to depose (take testimony from) the president," Davis said.

Jones accuses Clinton of making unwanted advances toward her in 1991 when he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state employee. Clinton denies the allegations. The Supreme Court made no ruling on the merits of her case, but said it should be allowed to proceed.
